decision.title: Clarify that timeout parameter is per-phase and not a total deadline
decision.rationale: While the advanced user documentation already explained this behavior, the inline API docstrings accessed via IDE tooltips and help() lacked this detail, causing user confusion. Updating the docstrings aligns inline documentation with existing prose without requiring code changes.
decision.decision_made: Expand the docstrings for the timeout parameter on requests.api.request() and Session.request() to explicitly clarify that a single float value applies to both connect and read phases independently, that it is not a total deadline, and that None means wait forever.
decision.problem_context: Issue #7350 reported that the docstring for the timeout parameter in requests is confusing, leading users to incorrectly expect a single float value to act as a total wall-clock deadline for the entire request rather than being applied independently to both connect and read phases.

pull_requests.title: docs: clarify timeout parameter is per-phase, not total deadline
pull_requests.body:
**Repo:** psf/requests (⭐ 52000)
**Type:** docs
**Files changed:** 2
**Lines:** +6/-2

## What
Expands the docstring for the `timeout` parameter on `requests.api.request()` and
`Session.request()` to spell out that a single float value is applied to both
the connect and read phases independently, that it is *not* a wall-clock
deadline for the whole request, and that `None` means wait forever.

## Why
Issue #7350 reports that the docstring for `timeout` is confusing: users
expect a single value to be a total request deadline. The longer-form docs
(`docs/user/advanced.rst`) already explain this, but the API docstrings —
which are what most users read via `help()` / IDE tooltips — did not. This
keeps the change small and aligns the inline docs with the existing prose
documentation.

## Testing
Pure docstring change, no behavior change. Verified rendering keeps reST
indentation valid (matches surrounding `:param:` blocks). No tests added or
needed.

## Risk
Low — documentation only, no code paths touched.

superseded_by.title: Treat None-valued method cookies as removals in dictionaries and sessions
superseded_by.rationale: Allows callers to explicitly unset or remove cookies by setting their value to None, matching expected HTTP client behavior and resolving issues with persistent session cookies.
superseded_by.decision_made: Treat None values in cookie dictionaries as removals, removing session cookies that are explicitly unset by request-level cookie dictionaries and omitting None values in helper functions.
superseded_by.problem_context: Passing None-valued cookies in request or session cookie dictionaries resulted in attempting to serialize invalid cookies instead of treating them as an explicit instruction to remove the cookie.

decision.title: Require load_default_certs() for custom HTTPAdapter SSL contexts
decision.rationale: The change was introduced as part of a CVE fix that tightened SSL context handling. Explicitly loading default certificates ensures that the context has the necessary CA bundle for verification, preventing silent failures and improving security posture.
decision.decision_made: Custom HTTPAdapter implementations must explicitly call ssl_context.load_default_certs() (or equivalent) to load system default certificates.
decision.problem_context: In Requests 2.32.3, custom HTTPAdapter SSL contexts no longer load system default certificates, causing SSL verification failures for users who rely on the previous implicit loading behavior.

issues.title: Certificate loading regression with HTTPAdapters in 2.32.3
issues.body:
<!-- Summary. -->

It appears that in version `2.32.3` default certificates are no longer loaded for custom `HTTPAdapter` contexts when they were previously.

I guess this might be a duplicate/related to https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/6726#issuecomment-2138406456.
Also related to https://github.com/psf/requests/pull/6710#issuecomment-2137802782 - adding `load_default_certs()` resolves the issue, but this wasn't required in previous versions and thus makes upgrading to `2.32.3` breaking.

## Expected Result

<!-- What you expected. -->

With the code below using `requests` version `2.32.2` I get the URL content with no error.

## Actual Result

<!-- What happened instead. -->

Using `2.32.3` I get:
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: HTTPSConnectionPool(host='raw.githubusercontent.com', port=443): Max retries exceeded with url: /psf/requests/main/MANIFEST.in (Caused by SSLError(SSLCertVerificationError(1, '[SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1006)')))
```

## Reproduction Steps

```python
import requests
import ssl
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter, DEFAULT_POOLBLOCK
from urllib3.util.ssl_ import create_urllib3_context

# adapted from https://github.com/IBM/python-sdk-core/blob/1c207385de627df5d12fd0a0ebd04717ce5bb29d/ibm_cloud_sdk_core/utils.py#L34
class SSLHTTPAdapter(HTTPAdapter):
    """Wraps the original HTTP adapter and adds additional SSL context."""

    def init_poolmanager(self, connections, maxsize, block=DEFAULT_POOLBLOCK, **pool_kwargs):
        """Create and use custom SSL configuration."""

        ssl_context = create_urllib3_context()
        ssl_context.minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2
        # ssl_context.load_default_certs() # Adding this resolves the certificate issue but it was not required before

        super().init_poolmanager(connections, maxsize, block, ssl_context=ssl_context, **pool_kwargs)

session = requests.Session()
http_adapter = SSLHTTPAdapter()
session.mount('https://', http_adapter)

print(session.get(url='https://raw.githubusercontent.com/psf/requests/main/MANIFEST.in').text)
```

superseded_by.title: Analyze session lifecycle and connection pooling in requests/adapters.py
superseded_by.rationale: urllib3's internal connection pooling handles connection cleanup properly, making explicit context management redundant in this specific architectural path.
superseded_by.decision_made: Determine that the finding is a minor observation and rely on urllib3's existing connection pooling mechanisms for cleanup.
superseded_by.problem_context: Static analysis indicated that urlopen() return value in requests/adapters.py is assigned to resp without an explicit context manager or .close(), posing a potential connection leak if responses are not fully consumed.

supersedes.title: Avoid reloading root certificates to improve concurrent performance
supersedes.rationale: Caching reduces I/O and CPU overhead, improving throughput and reducing latency in concurrent requests.
supersedes.decision_made: Cache root certificates and avoid reloading them on each request.
supersedes.problem_context: Reloading root certificates on each request caused performance bottlenecks in concurrent environments.

decision.title: Add practical timeout usage example and clarify exception raising in quickstart documentation
decision.rationale: Providing concrete, standard usage examples alongside failure cases helps developers correctly implement defensive networking practices in production code.
decision.decision_made: Updated the quickstart documentation to include a normal timeout usage example, clearer wording preceding the failure example, and explicit mention that Requests raises `Timeout`.
decision.problem_context: The quickstart documentation recommended using timeouts in production but lacked a practical example of a normal timeout value and clear explicit mention of the exception raised, making it harder for readers to apply correctly.

pull_requests.title: docs(quickstart): add practical timeout example
pull_requests.body:
## What changed

This updates the Quickstart timeout section to add:

- a practical example using a normal timeout value
- clearer wording before the failure example
- explicit mention that Requests raises `Timeout`

## Why

The section recommends using timeouts in production, so adding a normal usage example makes the guidance easier for readers to apply in real code.

decision.title: Add type hints to requests library
decision.rationale: Type hints improve code readability, enable better IDE autocomplete and error checking, and help developers write safer code without runtime performance penalties.
decision.decision_made: Introduce comprehensive type hints across the requests codebase.
decision.problem_context: The requests library lacked type hints, making it harder for developers to write well-typed and maintainable code that leverages modern IDE support and static analysis.

issues.title: Type hint needed
issues.body: Type hint helps to write better code, but in requests there's basically none

superseded_by.title: Change headers type hint to accept bytes values
superseded_by.rationale: The change enables callers to pass byte-encoded header values, which are supported by the underlying urllib3 library and may be required for certain use cases. It also aligns the type hint with the actual runtime behavior of the library.
superseded_by.decision_made: Updated the type hint for the headers parameter in requests.post (and related request methods) to MutableMapping[str, str | bytes] | None, allowing header values to be either str or bytes.
superseded_by.problem_context: Mypy warns about incompatible type for the headers argument in requests.post when using requests 2.34.1, because the type hint for headers was updated to a stricter signature.

decision.title: Clarify timeout behavior in quickstart documentation
decision.rationale: Improving documentation clarity prevents user confusion and reduces support overhead regarding how timeout parameters function under the hood.
decision.decision_made: Added a clarification to the quickstart admonition block in docs/user/quickstart.rst explaining that a single float applies to both connect and read timeouts independently, and that a tuple can be used to set them separately, along with a cross-reference to the advanced timeouts section.
decision.problem_context: Users misunderstood the timeout note in the quickstart guide, believing the timeout value applied to the entire response download rather than applying to connect and read independently.

pull_requests.title: docs(quickstart): clarify timeout applies to connect and read separately
pull_requests.body:
The quickstart timeout note explains that `timeout` is not a time limit on the entire response download, but does not mention that a single float applies to both connect and read timeouts independently, or that a `(connect_timeout, read_timeout)` tuple can set them separately.

Added a brief clarification to the existing admonition block in `docs/user/quickstart.rst` with a cross-reference to the advanced timeouts section, which already documents this behavior in detail.

Fixes #7350
